segmente.text: Let's play a game to see if you really understand marketing and branding.
Here are two bottles of red wine.
Option 1 costs $7 and you can buy it at Walmart.
Option 2 costs $150 and is only sold in selected stores.
The first bottle looks like every other wine on the shelf.
The second bottle has a thinner shape and comes in a wooden box.
Now be honest, which one would you assume is higher quality?
The answer is, they are equal.
It's the same wine that comes from the same company produced from the same grapes.
What creates this difference is not the product itself.
It's the experience and the feeling that lets the $150 wine appear to be of better quality and value.
And even though in reality the wine itself has the same quality,
to many people that experience is worth the extra money.
